Predict biomass from canopy cover

Source: R/kb_predict_cover_calibration.R
kb_predict_cover_calibration.Rd

Predict the expected wet biomass (kg/m²) of a plot from its plot cover.

Usage

kb_predict_cover_calibration(
  fit,
  new_data = NULL,
  ...,
  new_levels = c("average", "sample"),
  representative_site = NULL,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  estimate = stats::median,
  sig_fig = 3
)

Arguments

fit

A kb_fit_cover_calibration object.

new_data

A data frame of the rows to predict at, with canopy_area_m2 (the canopy area in the plot, m²), plot_area_m2 (the plot area, m²), canopy_tide_height_m (the tide height, m), and optionally site and year, or NULL for the observed surveys. year may be numeric or character: 2022 and "2022" match the same fitted year.

...

These dots are for future extensions and must be empty.

new_levels

A string giving how uncertainty is estimated for a site or year not in the data used to fit the model, or when new_data has no site or year column. Sites and years in the model fit always use their own estimates. One of:

  • "average" (the default): the typical site or year. The site and year effects are set to 0, their mean, so the interval does not include among-site or among-year variation. Use it to describe an average site or year.

  • "sample": a new effect for each new site or year, drawn from the estimated variation among sites or among years (the random-effect standard deviation). The point estimate is equivalent, but the interval is wider since it also includes that variation. Use it to get realistic uncertainty about a particular site or year that the model has no information on. Rows that name the same new site or year, or that have no site or year column, share one effect; give new sites or years different names for independent effects. The interval varies slightly between calls; use set.seed() to reproduce it.

representative_site

A character vector of sites in the fit whose effects a new site adopts (averaged when several are named), or NULL (the default) to follow new_levels.

conf_level

A number greater than 0 and less than 1 giving the compatibility-interval level.

estimate

A function that reduces a numeric vector of posterior draws to a single estimate, such as median or mean.

sig_fig

A whole number of significant figures for summary output.

Value

A kb_predictions object: the rows of new_data with cover_support (when the rows have a site and year), estimate, lower, and upper.

Details

Cover is tide-corrected and capped at full cover, 100% (see Methods). A warning is given if a row with canopy has a tide height above 2 m. When the fit has a presence part (when any survey in its data counted no plants), the prediction includes the probability that the plot holds plants.

See also

kb_new_data() to build rows by site or year over tide-corrected cover.

Other prediction functions: autoplot.kb_predictions(), kb_new_data(), kb_plot_predictions(), kb_predict_biomass_canopy(), kb_predict_biomass_in_situ(), kb_predict_carbon(), kb_predict_mean_weight(), kb_predict_nitrogen(), kb_predict_size(), kb_predict_weight(), kb_predict_wetdry(), predict.kb_fit_carbon(), predict.kb_fit_cover_calibration(), predict.kb_fit_nitrogen(), predict.kb_fit_size(), predict.kb_fit_weight(), predict.kb_fit_wetdry()

Examples

fit <- fit_cover_calibration_sim_nereo

# At the observed surveys
kb_predict_cover_calibration(fit)
#> <kb_predictions> predictor: cover | response: biomass_kg_m2 | by: site, year
#> # A tibble: 54 × 16
#>    survey_id       site  year  survey_area_m2 plants plot_area_m2 canopy_area_m2
#>    <chr>           <fct> <fct>          <dbl>  <int>        <dbl>          <dbl>
#>  1 otter_cove-202… otte… 2020            140     992         215            87.3
#>  2 otter_cove-202… otte… 2020             80     297         262.          110. 
#>  3 gull_rock-2020… gull… 2020            233.    660         233.           30.3
#>  4 cedar_bay-2020… ceda… 2020             40       0         270.           34.3
#>  5 cedar_bay-2020… ceda… 2020            180     861         255.           81.2
#>  6 heron_reef-202… hero… 2020            120     550         217.           73.5
#>  7 urchin_shoal-2… urch… 2020            160    1815         218.          116. 
#>  8 sculpin_head-2… scul… 2020            193.   1245         193.           30.1
#>  9 eagle_spit-202… eagl… 2020            200     471         259.           97.3
#> 10 tidepool_bluff… tide… 2020            180     698         229            62.3
#> # ℹ 44 more rows
#> # ℹ 9 more variables: canopy_tide_height_m <dbl>, weight_support <chr>,
#> #   size_support <chr>, biomass_kg_m2 <dbl>, biomass_sd_kg_m2 <dbl>,
#> #   cover_support <chr>, estimate <dbl>, lower <dbl>, upper <dbl>

# Curves over tide-corrected cover by site
kb_predict_cover_calibration(fit, kb_new_data(fit, by = "site"))
#> <kb_predictions> predictor: cover | response: biomass_kg_m2 | by: site
#> # A tibble: 270 × 8
#>    site   cover canopy_area_m2 plot_area_m2 canopy_tide_height_m estimate  lower
#>    <fct>  <dbl>          <dbl>        <dbl>                <dbl>    <dbl>  <dbl>
#>  1 otte… 0              0                 1                    0    0.148 0.0139
#>  2 otte… 0.0345         0.0345            1                    0    0.39  0.205 
#>  3 otte… 0.0690         0.0690            1                    0    0.658 0.432 
#>  4 otte… 0.103          0.103             1                    0    0.931 0.648 
#>  5 otte… 0.138          0.138             1                    0    1.2   0.877 
#>  6 otte… 0.172          0.172             1                    0    1.47  1.08  
#>  7 otte… 0.207          0.207             1                    0    1.73  1.28  
#>  8 otte… 0.241          0.241             1                    0    2     1.49  
#>  9 otte… 0.276          0.276             1                    0    2.26  1.69  
#> 10 otte… 0.310          0.310             1                    0    2.52  1.89  
#> # ℹ 260 more rows
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: upper <dbl>

# At new surveys, including a new site
kb_predict_cover_calibration(
  fit,
  data.frame(
    site = c("otter_cove", "new_site"),
    canopy_area_m2 = 80,
    plot_area_m2 = 200,
    canopy_tide_height_m = 0.5
  )
)
#> <kb_predictions> predictor: cover | response: biomass_kg_m2 | by: site
#> # A tibble: 2 × 7
#>   site     canopy_area_m2 plot_area_m2 canopy_tide_height_m estimate lower upper
#>   <chr>             <dbl>        <dbl>                <dbl>    <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 otter_c…             80          200                  0.5     3.65  2.73  4.86
